cause_quote: It subscribed the widget to gateway events and, whenever `!state.view` and a `chat` event reached state `final`/`aborted`/`error` for the session, ran `forgetPendingCanvasView(binding); activeBinding = undefined; reconcile();`, re-requesting even widgets that had already failed terminally.
user_saw: An old chat with a missing Canvas widget kept offering Retry and re-requested the failed view on every later chat event or remount, and those requests scanned the transcript and slowed other users' history reads.
summary: Control UI now keeps terminal Canvas widget failures across remounts and later chat events and caps transient retries with exponential backoff; the server reads the document before the transcript receipt scan and marks sandbox-host startup failures retryable.
reasoning: The event-driven re-read that floods history reads was added by #175025 (pending/access-denied/host-failure states) and fired for any widget without a view, including terminal unavailable errors; later refactors (#176457, #183467) only moved this logic into the loader/owner modules. The fix also bundles a server-side ordering optimization and a sandbox-failure classification, so the single cause is medium confidence.
